contents.name: §3.1: uniform-state perturbations and high-frequency propagation parameters

source_review.read_extent: Retrieved the full 25-page paper and read the complete small-perturbation and high-frequency-speed discussion in §3.1, PDF p. 8, including equations (3.5)–(3.6) and the following qualification.
source_review.supports: An independent treatment connects uniform-state perturbations and model-dependent high-frequency propagation parameters to causal restrictions.
source_review.limitations: The source treats a broader zero-charge viscous gradient model, including shear, and its group-speed argument is not the finite-propagation theorem used here. The exact perfect linear branch is proved conditionally by the local supplier.

contents.name: §3.1: bulk relaxation contribution to the longitudinal speed

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete high-frequency longitudinal propagation formula and its stated natural-unit and short-wavelength scope in §3.1, PDF p. 8.
source_review.supports: The bulk relaxation ratio contributes to the model-specific longitudinal propagation condition.
source_review.limitations: Its full formula also contains shear terms and uses a different constitutive framework. It does not establish this postulate's restricted bulk-only speed or finite propagation.

source_review.read_extent: Read the entropy-current introduction and its conformal-fluid divergence analysis in §4.1, PDF pp. 9–11.
source_review.supports: Context that non-equilibrium entropy currents can have second-order corrections and that positivity imposes model-specific coefficient conditions.
source_review.limitations: The source explicitly limits its entropy-current discussion and does not supply the exact variable-coefficient corrected bulk law adopted by the supplier. No measurements or experimental verification are claimed.

contents.name: §§1.4.2–1.5: transient bulk relaxation and extended entropy current

source_review.read_extent: Retrieved and inspected the complete 148-page lecture-note PDF. source_review.supports: An independent full lecture treatment of dynamical bulk relaxation variables and second-order entropy-current corrections.
source_review.limitations: The source's Israel–Stewart equations contain their own coefficient relations and higher-order terms; they are not identified with the exact derivative-corrected law in the local bulk postulate. That law is adopted explicitly and its local entropy identity is proved separately.

contents.name: §1.4.2 and §2.5.4: causality and stability are model-dependent

source_review.read_extent: Read the statements about nonzero relaxation time and additional coefficient restrictions in §1.4.2, PDF p. 23, and the model-specific causality/stability discussion in §2.5.4, PDF pp. 52–53.
source_review.supports: Positive relaxation time alone does not ensure causality; the transport ratios and selected dynamics matter.
source_review.limitations: This is not the proof of the present branch's exact inequality. Its precise energy, speed, and finite-propagation claims follow only conditionally from the named mathematical carrier.
